ModifyMaxEnergy.rationale: Bread.cs:19-31 returns the amount unchanged when TurnNumber == 1 and otherwise adds EnergyVar('GainEnergy', 1).BaseValue; bread.py:19-21 is the same branch with the same constant. Consulted at player.py:163 = turn_structure step 17. The C# null-check on PlayerCombatState is defensive and has no sim counterpart to diverge from.

AfterSideTurnStart.rationale: Bread.cs:33-39 spends EnergyVar('LoseEnergy', 2).BaseValue on the owner's turn 1; bread.py:24-25 subtracts 2 on `self.turn == 1`. The slot is correct -- on_player_turn_started is the post-draw AfterSideTurnStart position (executed via the turn-order probe), which matters because the two halves of this relic must net to -1 energy on turn 1 and +1 thereafter, and both codebases apply the loss after the reset that ModifyMaxEnergy fed. Both constants read BaseValue, the non-ascension branch, and neither has an AscensionHelper call.

guards.what: N1: `PlayerCmd.LoseEnergy` (Bread.cs:37) vs the sim's direct `player.energy = max(0, player.energy - 2)` (bread.py:25)
guards.rationale: Unlike its sibling GainEnergy -- which runs Hook.ModifyEnergyGain and is why relic/booming_conch's direct assignment IS a divergence -- LoseEnergy dispatches NO hook: its whole body is two guards (`amount <= 0`, `CombatManager.IsEnding`) and a call to PlayerCombatState.LoseEnergy (PlayerCmd.cs:50-62). Neither guard can fire here (the amount is a constant 2 and turn-1 setup cannot run while combat is ending), so the direct subtraction is equivalent. The sim's max(0, ...) clamp matches the game's non-negative energy floor. Checked deliberately because the same shortcut in booming_conch is a recorded gap and the difference is entirely in which C# command was used.

The `player != base.Owner` / `shuffler == base.Owner` / `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Owner` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player. The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState), so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

guards.what: N4: the two DynamicVars are keyed ('GainEnergy', 'LoseEnergy') rather than using the default Energy key
guards.rationale: Both are EnergyVars with explicit keys because the relic has two energy numbers (Bread.cs:11-15); the sim uses two literals. Recorded because a keyed DynamicVar is read with `DynamicVars["Key"]` rather than `DynamicVars.Energy`, and misreading which key feeds which branch would silently swap 1 and 2.
